subject.title: [Feature]: Stabilize remote Codex app-server connections with a command-backed transport

question: Should OpenClaw add an experimental command-backed Codex app-server transport for SSH/proxy streams, or should remote Codex execution stay on the local-app-server direction tracked in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/101282?
rationale: This is not a narrow bug fix: it adds new config surface, runs an operator-configured command, changes app-server reconnect ownership, and relies on upstream WebSocket-over-Unix-socket proxy framing.

options.title: Design command-backed transport
options.body: Add a narrow experimental Codex plugin transport with no-shell command spawning, explicit incompatible-field validation, and live SSH/proxy proof before promotion.

options.title: Fold into local app-server remote execution
options.body: Treat this as an alternative to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/101282 and keep production remote work focused on Gateway-owned app-server plus authenticated remote exec environments.

options.title: Keep current WebSocket support only
options.body: Leave remote operators on configured WebSocket URLs or external SSH port-forwarding until stronger user demand or upstream support justifies another transport.

recommendation.title: Design command-backed transport
recommendation.body: Add a narrow experimental Codex plugin transport with no-shell command spawning, explicit incompatible-field validation, and live SSH/proxy proof before promotion.

likelyOwner.reason: The related protected remote-execution direction and recent app-server lifecycle work make this the best available product/security owner signal.
